title: Streamlined weights-to-runtime onboarding pathway for open LLMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a hardened, auditable pipeline that takes upstream open LLM weights through validation, conversion, profiling and publishes a pinned model version and performance profile into the Redwood model catalog. The goal is to reduce manual steps for new open-model intake from ~6 hours of manual engineer time to an automated flow that completes within a reproducible CI run and produces a signed artifact, a runtime-compatible bundle, and a performance profile JSON for the catalog.
steps: Ingest: accept HF/URL/manifest uploads and validate checksums + license metadata
Policy checks: run license classifier and embargo/usage policy scanner
Sanity tests: quick forward-pass smoke using minimal tokens to catch broken weights
Conversion: canonicalize into runtime-friendly format (optimum/torch->core runtime format) with quantization options
Artifact signing: produce provenance metadata and store a signed artifact in internal registry
Profiling: run standardized perf bench (latency P50/P95, throughput, memory, kv-cache behavior) across representative sequence lengths and batch shapes
Quality eval: run sample eval prompts and sanity generation checks against baseline metrics
Version pinning: publish a stable model version with pinned weight hash + conversion config
Publish: write performance profile and manifest to model catalog and generate rollout candidate
Rollout gating: create canary configuration for runtime teams with automatic fallback rules
test_plan: Unit: converter module conversions produce identical outputs within tolerance for reference ops
Integration: end-to-end CI job ingest->profile completes on ephemeral infra and artifacts uploaded
Regression: compare new performance profile against historical baselines for similar families
Load: run profiling job at expected production concurrency to validate autoscaler triggers
Security: run license and static scanner; verify KMS encryption for artifact at rest
